fields.reasoning: The finding and critic are right: the branch path in decision-main-writes-get-a-branch cuts model branches from origin/main and pushes them, so in a repo without origin no entry can ever be held by a model branch, and every write would be an orphan. Flagging those would turn rhiza check warnings and health bad (exit 1) across ~35 git-init testscripts (e.g. change-show-canonical-text.txtar, check-evidence-actor.txtar, health.txtar, health-projects.txtar), which the change set never intended. An orphan only means something when the remedy exists: commit-untracked needs a remote to push a branch and open a PR. The code already treats a missing origin/main as 'nothing to compare' (internal/api/health.go healthOriginAhead and the behind-origin facts skip silently when refs/remotes/origin/main does not resolve), so keying on the same ref is consistent and cheap, needs no fetch, and keeps a local-only project, where uncommitted entries are the owner's own working state, free of noise. The owner's words ('Everything should get it's own branch') concern a project's shared main, which presupposes a remote. Adding the no-origin case to both acceptances closes the gap the reviewer named.
fields.statement: Orphan reporting and committing apply only in a repo whose main checkout has origin/main (refs/remotes/origin/main resolves). In a repo with no origin/main (a testscript git-init repo, a local-only project) a main-checkout write keeps today's behaviour: it writes the entry and opens no model branch or PR, since there is nothing to cut from or push to; rhiza check gives no orphan warning and its output is unchanged; rhiza health's main-checkout part reports no orphan problem (its state is decided as today, untracked entries not counted); rhiza model commit-untracked and the daemon's sweep do nothing and say no origin/main exists. @{01M76FAABBDGMZA9F3BBBA3H0D}'s acceptance testscript (check-orphan-log.txtar) also asserts that the same untracked entry in a git-init repo with no origin gives no warning, and @{01M76FAA9ATEZ0372B4BZ9SRST}'s acceptance (TestHealthMainOrphanLog) also asserts that an untracked entry in a repo with no origin/main leaves the part ok; existing testscripts and goldens in git-init repos do not change.
